learn.title: Learn Ravenry
learn.lead: Short looks at what Ravenry adds to a session. “Try it” opens a session with a message ready for you to send; nothing runs until you do.
learn.panes.title: Panes beside your agent
learn.panes.line: Claude opens a terminal next to its own to run a server or a build, and you can watch or type in it.
learn.panes.message: Start this project in a Ravenry pane beside you and tell me what you see.
learn.needs.title: Needs you
learn.needs.line: When an agent waits on you, it goes to the top with its question; answer here or on your phone.
learn.needs.message: Ask me through Ravenry which of this project’s open TODOs to look at first, with two or three options.
learn.phone.title: Your phone
learn.phone.line: Pair it once and questions, picks and approvals reach you away from the desk.
learn.pick.title: Pick between pictures
learn.pick.line: An agent shows two to four looks side by side; pick one or circle the part you mean.
learn.pick.message: Sketch three quick ideas for this project as pictures in a scratch folder, don’t touch the code, and let me pick one in Ravenry.
learn.review.title: Review and merge
learn.review.line: A session working on its own copy of the code shows what it changed, and you merge it when it is right.
learn.review.message: Work on your own copy of this project and fix one small thing you find. I’ll review it in Ravenry before it’s merged.
learn.film.title: The filmstrip
learn.film.line: Scrub back through what a terminal showed, to see what happened while you were away.
learn.decisions.title: Decisions
learn.decisions.line: What you told an agent is kept word for word, so the next session follows it too.
learn.decisions.message: From now on, keep commit messages to one line. Record that as my decision in Ravenry.
learn.filmNeeds: The filmstrip needs a terminal with some history: open one and use it a little first.
learn.noBoard: Try it starts a session through Ravenry’s board, which is not running.
learn.noAssistant: Try it needs Claude Code or Codex on this Mac.
learn.onClipboard: The message is on the clipboard: paste it when the assistant is ready.

rep.offHint: Off. Turned on, once a day it reads what you typed to Claude Code and Codex, with at most 3 calls to the assistant new sessions start with, and the Rules page offers a rule for a correction you made three times.
rep.onHint: Once a day, at most 3 calls. A rule is written only when you add it, after a dated backup of the rules file.
rep.ranFailed: The last run, {when}, did not finish. It is tried again in 6 hours.
rep.locked: Set by MC_REPEATS_AUTO when the board started.
ho.foot: Applies to every project. Saves as you change it.
ho.saved: Saved. Applies at each session’s next stop.
checkpoint.toldNo: {who} is told you said no, with your reason if you give one.
checkpoint.typedInto: Typed into {pane}, the program waiting there
checkpoint.toProgram: Goes straight to that program, not to {who}
checkpoint.toCommand: Goes straight to that command, not to {who}
checkpoint.notKept: Not kept in logs, history or on your phone
checkpoint.secretShort: That is too short for a secret.
checkpoint.secretLong: That is longer than a secret can be (4 KiB).
checkpoint.unknownKind: This version of Ravenry does not know this kind of question. You can only refuse it.
pick.circleTip: Drag a ring around a part of a picture
pick.otherMachine: This picture is on another machine.
pick.htmlPage: A page: open it from the board to see it.
lease.stillYours: What you type still goes in, marked as yours.
lease.canTypeSession: Can type until its session ends
lease.ownNote: Panes an agent opens are its own; it types there without asking.
review.unmerged: The merge is undone. Its copy is back on its branch.
review.discardAsk: This removes its copy and the branch {branch} without merging. Its changes are lost.
review.discarded: Discarded its copy and the branch {branch}.
review.asks: {who} is done and asks for a review
review.builtOn: Built in its own copy on {branch}.
review.afterLine: Merge removes the copy and keeps the branch
review.couldNotRead: The board could not read its work.
review.notKept: The board did not keep the comment.
files.sameFolder: Both are in the same folder, so whoever saves last wins.
files.ownCopy: Each has its own copy, so it shows when you merge.
files.none: No session changed a file yet.
files.note: An orange row is a file two sessions changed. "read" means it looked but did not change it.
start.heading: Start a session
start.lead: Pick a folder and an assistant. It opens in a real terminal here, and the list on the left keeps every session in order, the ones that need you first.
start.noAssistant: Neither Claude Code nor Codex is installed here yet. Install one, then come back. A plain shell works meanwhile.
start.modelNote: Remembered for this project. To switch during a session, type /model in it.
start.ownCopyB: It gets its own copy of the code
start.ownCopy: , on a new branch, because {topic} is already working in {project}. You review and merge it when it's done.
start.inFolderB: It works right in the folder
start.inFolder: , beside {topic}, so they share the files.
start.ownCopyLink: Give it its own copy instead
start.foot: Keeping cmux, iTerm2 or Rex? Ravenry still follows the sessions you run there.
start.local: The board is not running, so this runs in a pane of this window. The board follows it once it starts.
start.askingT: macOS is asking whether Ravenry may read {folder}. Click Allow in the dialog.
start.askingS: Closed the dialog? Open System Settings > Privacy & Security > Files & Folders, find Ravenry and turn on {folder}. The board starts by itself once it may read it.
start.denied: macOS did not let Ravenry read {folders}. Turn it on in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Files & Folders.
npm.title: You already run Ravenry from npm
npm.lead: The app can take over from it on the same data. Your sessions, ideas, plans, rules and settings stay as they are.
npm.same: It stops, and the app's hub starts on the same port.
npm.notRunning: The npm board{version} is not running
npm.notRunningS: The app's hub starts on its data and port.
npm.hooksS: Their hooks point at the app instead. Your other hooks and settings stay.
npm.noHooksS: The app offers its own when you start a session.
npm.loginS: That login start is turned off and kept, so going back turns it on again.
npm.noLoginS: When something does, it is turned off and kept, so going back turns it on again.
npm.copyFirst: A copy of everything is kept first
npm.foot: You can go back any time: {menu}, Go Back to the npm Board.
npm.stepLoginS: Kept, so going back turns it on again.
npm.stepBackup: A copy of your data is kept
npm.stepHooksS: Their settings files were backed up next to them.
npm.switchingLead: A few seconds. Sessions keep running; anything they report meanwhile waits in the event files.
npm.doneLead: The app runs your board now, at login too. The npm board is stopped and nothing starts it.
npm.barAgain: Back on the npm board. Start it as before:
npm.barBackDown: Back on the npm board. Start it as you did before.
npm.barKeeps: Your npm board runs this data, so the app shows it and starts no hub of its own.
npm.backTitle: Go back to the npm board?
npm.backBusy: Going back to the npm board...
npm.backLead: The app's hub stops and no longer starts at login.
npm.backLi1: Claude Code's and Codex's hooks go back to the npm board
npm.backLi2: ideas made here are written back where it reads them
npm.backLi3: your sessions, plans, rules and settings stay
npm.backLogin: Its login start is turned on again, which starts it.
npm.backByHand: You started the npm board yourself, so start it again the same way once this is done.
npm.ptrWhy: {what} needs the app's own hub, which does not run while the npm board keeps your data.
npm.ptrUp: Your board is the npm board
npm.ptrDown: Your npm board is not running
npm.ptrFoot: Switching to the app keeps every session, idea, plan, rule and setting, and can be undone.
npm.onBoard: Do it on the npm board
npm.onBoardS2: and starts sessions in your terminal, as before.
npm.shellsS: A plain shell in this window needs no hub.
npm.startAgainS: in the terminal where you ran it. Its sessions show up here once it answers.
menu.npmBack: Go Back to the npm Board…
update.title: Updates
update.devBuild: This is a development build. It does not update itself.
update.noSource: This build does not say where its updates come from.
update.unsigned: This build is not signed for a team, so it cannot check that an update comes from the same place. It does not update itself.
update.downloadingS: It installs when you quit Ravenry. Your sessions keep running through the update.
update.readyS: Restart Ravenry to use it. Your sessions keep running: they are not part of the window.
update.stopped: The update to {version} did not start after 3 tries ({why}), so Ravenry keeps the hub that runs now.
update.noAnswer: the new hub did not answer
update.why.noFeed: The newest release has no build of this app.
update.why.badFeed: The release's update file could not be read.
update.why.checksum: The download did not match the release (SHA-256 {got}..., the release says {want}...), so nothing was replaced.
update.why.unzip: The download could not be opened, so nothing was replaced.
update.why.signature: The new version's signature did not check out ({why}), so nothing was replaced.
update.why.team: The new version is signed by team {theirs}, not {ours}, so nothing was replaced.
update.why.notRavenry: The download is not Ravenry, so nothing was replaced.
update.why.version: The download is version {got}, not {want}, so nothing was replaced.
update.why.folder: Ravenry cannot replace itself in {folder}. Move it to a folder you can write to, or download the new version from the releases page.
command.title: Make ravenry in your terminals Ravenry's?
command.nowOther: Typing ravenry in a terminal runs {what}, which knows none of the commands agents use (ravenry pick, ravenry ask and the rest).
command.nowNone: Typing ravenry in a terminal finds nothing now, so agents have to type its whole path.
command.adds: Ravenry links {link} to its own command.
command.addsWithLine: Ravenry links {link} to its own command and adds two lines at the end of {rc} (backed up first) so the link comes first.
command.after: New terminals use it. The npm board's own commands still work, and this menu takes it out again.
command.done: ravenry in a new terminal is Ravenry's now.
command.failed: The ravenry command did not change: {why}
command.blocked: {link} is another program, so Ravenry leaves it alone. Move it away, then try again.
command.removeDetail: Ravenry takes out {link}. Agents still reach Ravenry through its skill.
command.removeWithLine: Ravenry takes out {link} and its two lines in {rc}. Agents still reach Ravenry through its skill.
command.removed: The ravenry command is gone. New terminals no longer run Ravenry's.
command.offer: ravenry in your terminals runs {what}, so the Ravenry commands agents type fail there.
uninstall.title: Uninstall Ravenry?
uninstall.detail: Ravenry takes out its hooks in Claude Code and Codex, its skill, the board's background service, the ravenry command and its program files. Each file it changed is put back as it was, or backed up first. Terminals open now keep running until they end. Your projects and their briefs stay.
uninstall.purge: Also delete Ravenry's own data: ideas, pages, decisions and settings
uninstall.finish: To finish, move Ravenry to the Trash: it shows in Finder when you quit.
strip.closeSession: Close the tab (the session goes on)
split.dividerTip: Drag to resize, double-click to even
pane.alone: It is the only pane in this tab
pane.tooNarrow: Too narrow to split: each pane needs at least {pt} points across
pane.tooShort: Too short to split: each pane needs at least {pt} points of height
term.daemonStopped: the Ravenry that ran it stopped
find.caseOld: Match case needs a newer daemon. New tabs have it.
find.regexOld: Regular expressions need a newer daemon. New tabs have them.
strip.film: The last 20 seconds of this pane
film.title: Last 20 seconds
film.nothing: It drew nothing new in that time.
film.noDaemon: No daemon here holds that pane.
film.whyLost: the connection to the daemon closed
film.whySlow: the daemon took too long to answer
film.whyDaemon: the daemon could not draw the pane
film.whyBig: the pane is too big to picture; try again in a smaller window
film.showing: Showing {time}, {s} s ago. The pane is still running underneath.
film.nearestBefore: No picture was kept of that moment; this is the closest one, {s} s before it.
film.nearestAfter: No picture was kept of that moment; this is the closest one, {s} s after it.

setup.title: Let {who} work with Ravenry
setup.lead: One step before {who} opens in {folder}. Both are on; you can change either later in Settings.
setup.hooksP: {who}’s sessions tell Ravenry when they ask you something, finish or hand off, so they move to Needs you and can alert you.
setup.hooksNeeds: Needs Ravenry’s board running; Settings can do it later.
setup.skillP: {who} can open panes beside it, read their screens, show you pictures to pick from, and ask you through the board and your phone. The skill runs
setup.skillP2: , so it always matches this version.
setup.foot: Each file is backed up first, and your other hooks and skills stay as they are.
setup.hooksFailed: Could not set up the hooks: {why}
